title: Sitarist Rishab Rikhiram Sharma Sets Sights on Oscar for Ramayana Song
excerpt: The 27-year-old sitarist, now confirmed as a contributor to the Ramayana film's music alongside Hans Zimmer and A.R. Rahman, says he believes the epic's soundtrack could bring India another Academy Award.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Rishab Rikhiram Sharma aims for an Oscar with the Ramayana film's song 'Rama Rama'.
  • The ₹4,000-crore Ramayana film features music by Hans Zimmer and A.R. Rahman.
  • Sharma performed live at the Delhi trailer launch on July 18, confirming his soundtrack role.
  • The film is set for a Diwali 2026 release, with global ambitions including IMAX screenings.
  • Sitarist Rishab Rikhiram Sharma has expressed his aspiration for an Oscar win through the Ramayana film's song 'Rama Rama,' in which he contributes sitar performances alongside composers Hans Zimmer and A.R. Rahman.
  • Producer Namit Malhotra confirmed Sharma's involvement in the Ramayana soundtrack at the film's grand Delhi trailer launch on July 18, where the sitarist performed live.
  • The ₹4,000-crore two-part epic, starring Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi, and Yash, is set for a Diwali 2026 release with global theatrical ambitions including IMAX.
  • Sharma's remarks align with growing industry sentiment that Ramayana's music, created by two Oscar-winning composers, could contend at the Academy Awards.

Rishab Rikhiram Sharma, the 27-year-old sitarist who has spent the past year filling 20,000-seat arenas across India, has declared his ambition squarely: he wants the Ramayana film's song 'Rama Rama' to win an Oscar.

The statement, reported by India Today, came days after producer Namit Malhotra confirmed at the film's grand Delhi trailer launch on July 18 that Sharma would be contributing his sitar to the Ramayana soundtrack—placing him alongside two of the most decorated composers in global cinema, Hans Zimmer and A.R. Rahman.

From Arena Tours to the Oscar Stage

Sharma's path to one of the most anticipated Indian film projects in history has been unconventional. The Delhi-born, New York-based musician comes from the Rikhi Ram family, whose instrument workshop in Connaught Place has supplied sitars to legends from Ravi Shankar to George Harrison since the 1920s. Sharma is the first performer in the family's lineage.

Trained under Pandit Ravi Shankar—a connection that has been both celebrated and publicly debated—Sharma built his reputation through a blend of classical ragas and electronic production that has drawn comparisons to no existing template. His 'Sitar for Mental Health' India Tour 2026, a 10-city run that concluded in April, drew between 10,000 and 20,000 attendees per show and attracted audiences ranging from Deepika Padukone to Kumar Mangalam Birla.

"The Oscars, the Grammys… I feel like the African-American community had their moment. Now it's the brown moment. Indians, South Asians are making their mark."

— Rishab Rikhiram Sharma, in an interview with Grazia India

A Song Built for the Global Stage

The Ramayana film has been constructed with exactly such global ambitions. Directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Malhotra's Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG—the eight-time Oscar-winning VFX studio—the two-part epic carries a reported budget of ₹4,000 crore, making it the most expensive Indian production to date.

Ranbir Kapoor plays Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi stars as Sita, and Kannada superstar Yash takes on the role of Ravana, with Sunny Deol as Hanuman. The musical score pairs A.R. Rahman's songs and Indian musical sensibility with Hans Zimmer's orchestral work—a collaboration that Reuters has described as giving the film "a visual and auditory edge" designed to compete globally.

Kumar Vishwas, the poet and lyricist who wrote the film's songs, shared an anecdote at the Delhi trailer launch about a recording session for a Ram-Sita swayamvar song where Shreya Ghoshal sang while Rahman and Zimmer worked together late into the night, according to Bollywood Hungama.

Part One is scheduled for release during Diwali 2026, with Part Two following in Diwali 2027. The makers are planning to showcase the film at San Diego Comic-Con on July 23—only the second Indian film, after Kalki 2898 AD, to receive a presentation at the event.

The Diaspora Connection

Sharma's involvement carries particular resonance for Indians abroad. Based in New York, he has performed at the White House Diwali celebration and the Howdy Modi event in Houston, building a profile that bridges the diaspora's cultural pride with mainstream global recognition.

His aspiration for an Oscar is not without precedent in the Ramayana ecosystem. Casting director Mukesh Chhabra has previously stated he believes the film "could go all the way to the Oscars," while the involvement of Zimmer—a two-time Academy Award winner for The Lion King and Dune—and Rahman, who won two Oscars for Slumdog Millionaire, gives the film's soundtrack genuine contention in the Best Original Song and Best Original Score categories.

What's Next

The worldwide trailer premiere for Ramayana is set for July 24, 2026. For Sharma, the ELLE India Award winner who once told The Hollywood Reporter India that he "stopped dreaming because even when you dream, you fall short of what the universe has to offer," the Oscar ambition represents a new chapter—one where the sitar, an instrument his family has built for a century, could echo through the Dolby Theatre.
